blocks.text: **National income** measures the total value of goods and services produced by an economy in a year. Its core aggregates — **GDP, GNP, NNP, National Income (NNP at factor cost)** — and the distinction between **market price and factor cost, nominal and real** — are fundamental macroeconomic concepts.

rows: Value of final goods/services produced **within a country** in a year.
GDP **+ net factor income from abroad (NFIA)**.
**NNP at factor cost** (NNP at market price – indirect taxes + subsidies).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: national income concepts

rows: Value of all final goods & services produced within a country in a year (domestic).
GDP + net factor income from abroad (NFIA).
GNP − depreciation; **NNP at factor cost = National Income**.
GDP − (net product taxes); output by sector (India now headlines **GVA & GDP**).

items: **Market price vs factor cost**: FC = MP − indirect taxes + subsidies.
**Methods of measuring**: **Product/Value-added, Income, Expenditure** methods — all give the same GDP.
**Real vs Nominal GDP**: real = constant prices (removes inflation); **GDP deflator** = nominal/real ×100.
**Base year** currently **2011-12** (revised methodology 2015); **MoSPI/CSO/NSO** compiles.
GNP = GDP + NFIA; NNP = GNP – depreciation; NI = NNP at factor cost.
Real GDP adjusts for inflation; GDP deflator = nominal/real ×100.

prelimsPointers: **GDP** — output produced **within domestic territory**; **GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad**.
**NNP = GNP – Depreciation**; **National Income = NNP at factor cost**.
**Market price = factor cost + indirect taxes – subsidies**.
**Nominal GDP** at current prices; **Real GDP** at constant (base-year) prices.
**GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100** — a measure of inflation.
**Per-capita income = National Income / Population**.
**Green GNP** accounts for environmental degradation.
**GNP = GDP + NFIA**; **NNP = GNP − depreciation**; **National Income = NNP at factor cost**.
**FC = MP − indirect taxes + subsidies**; three methods (product/income/expenditure) give same GDP.
**Real GDP** = constant prices; **GDP deflator** = nominal/real ×100.
India's national-accounts base year = **2011-12**; compiled by **NSO/MoSPI**.
mainsAngles: Explain the concepts of GDP, GNP and National Income.

glossary.definition: Gross Domestic Product — value of final goods/services produced within a country in a year.
Net Factor Income from Abroad — the difference added to GDP to get GNP.
GDP measured at constant prices, adjusted for inflation.

blocks.text: India's **national accounts** are compiled by the **National Statistical Office (NSO/MoSPI)** using three approaches (**production, income, expenditure**). Estimates use a **base year** (currently 2011-12), and GDP is now reported at **market prices** with **Gross Value Added (GVA)** by sector.

rows: **GDP = GVA + taxes on products – subsidies**; GVA measures sectoral output.
First national-income estimate by **Dadabhai Naoroji**; scientific by **V.K.R.V. Rao**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: India's national accounts

items: **System of National Accounts (SNA)**; India moved to **GVA-based** measurement (2015) with base **2011-12**; **NSO (National Statistical Office)** under MoSPI publishes GDP estimates (advance, provisional, revised).
**Sectoral shares (approx.)**: Agriculture & allied ~**18% of GVA**, Industry ~**28%**, Services ~**54%**; but employment shares are skewed toward agriculture.
**Savings & investment**: Gross Domestic Savings & GFCF (Gross Fixed Capital Formation) drive growth; household is the biggest saver; **ICOR** (incremental capital-output ratio) measures efficiency.
**Indices**: **IIP** (industrial output), **CPI/WPI** (inflation), **PMI**, **eight core industries**; India's data reforms (PLFS for jobs, GST data).
NSO/MoSPI compiles; three methods; base year 2011-12; GVA by sector.
First scientific national income estimate = V.K.R.V. Rao.

prelimsPointers: National accounts compiled by the **National Statistical Office (NSO), MoSPI** (merger of CSO & NSSO).
Three methods — **production/value-added, income, expenditure**.
Current **base year = 2011-12**.
**GVA (Gross Value Added)** = GDP at basic prices; **GDP = GVA + product taxes – subsidies**.
First national-income estimate — **Dadabhai Naoroji** ('Poverty and Un-British Rule'); first scientific — **V.K.R.V. Rao**.
**National Sample Survey (NSS)** provides consumption/employment data.
The **Economic Survey** & **Union Budget** use these accounts.
India uses **GVA**-based accounting; base year **2011-12**; agency = **NSO/MoSPI**.
GVA shares: **Services ~54%, Industry ~28%, Agriculture ~18%**.
**IIP** = industrial output; **eight core industries** ~40% of IIP weight.
**GFCF & Gross Domestic Savings** drive growth; **ICOR** = capital efficiency.
mainsAngles: Describe how India's national income is estimated.

glossary.definition: The National Statistical Office (MoSPI) that compiles India's national accounts.
Gross Value Added — sectoral output at basic prices, the building block of GDP.
The reference year (currently 2011-12) for computing real (constant-price) national income.

blocks.text: India faces intertwined **demographic, poverty and inequality** challenges — a large young population (dividend or burden), persistent though declining **poverty**, and widening **income and regional inequality** — central concerns of inclusive development.

rows: Large working-age share (~2005-2055 window); needs jobs, skills, health.
**Tendulkar & Rangarajan committees**; **NITI Aayog MPI** (health, education, living standards).
Measured by the **Gini coefficient** & **Lorenz curve**; rising wealth concentration.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: demography, poverty & inequality

items: **Demographic dividend**: rising working-age share (~2018-2055 window); needs jobs, skills, health to reap; else 'demographic disaster'.
**Poverty estimation**: **Alagh → Lakdawala → Tendulkar (2009) → Rangarajan (2014)** committees; now **NITI National MPI** (headcount + intensity).
**Inequality**: Gini; wealth concentration; regional (BIMARU vs south/west) & rural-urban gaps; gender.
**Population policy**: **NPP 2000** (TFR target 2.1 — achieved ~2.0, NFHS-5); ageing to follow; NFHS data on health/nutrition.
**Global MPI (UNDP/OPHI)** shows India lifted ~415 million out of poverty (2005-21) — sharp decline.
Poverty lines: Tendulkar & Rangarajan committees; MPI (multidimensional).
Inequality: Gini coefficient / Lorenz curve; demographic dividend window.

prelimsPointers: **Demographic dividend** window ~**2005-2055**; needs jobs & skilling.
Poverty-line committees — **Tendulkar (2009), Rangarajan (2014)**; earlier **Lakdawala, Alagh**.
**Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** — health, education, standard of living (NITI Aayog & UNDP/OPHI).
**Gini coefficient (0-1)** & the **Lorenz curve** measure income inequality.
Poverty in India has **declined** significantly (NITI MPI reports).
**Kuznets curve** — inequality rises then falls with development.
**Regional & rural-urban inequalities** remain significant.
Poverty committees: **Alagh → Lakdawala → Tendulkar (2009) → Rangarajan (2014)**; now **National MPI**.
**Demographic dividend** window ~2018-2055; India's **TFR ~2.0** (NFHS-5, below replacement).
Inequality via **Gini**; regional 'BIMARU' vs southern/western states.
**NPP 2000** target TFR **2.1** — achieved.
mainsAngles: Discuss poverty and inequality measurement in India.

glossary.definition: Growth potential from a large working-age population relative to dependents.
A poverty measure combining health, education and living-standard deprivations.
A 0-1 measure of income inequality, derived from the Lorenz curve.

blocks.text: India's **occupational structure** is shifting slowly from agriculture to services, but its **labour market** is marked by **informality, low female participation and various forms of unemployment** — measured through the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**.

rows: Falling primary share; rising services; but agriculture still largest employer (~45%).
**LFPR (labour force participation), WPR (worker-population ratio), UR (unemployment rate)**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: occupational structure & unemployment

items: **Types of unemployment**: **disguised** (surplus labour in agriculture — marginal productivity ~0), **seasonal**, **structural** (skill-demand mismatch), **cyclical** (demand-driven), **frictional**, **educated** unemployment, **underemployment**.
**Data**: **PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey, since 2017)** by NSO gives **LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate**; **CMIE** private data; **usual status vs current weekly status**.
**Concerns**: low & falling **female LFPR**, informalisation, jobless growth, gig/platform economy (**e-Shram** portal), skilling gap.
**Formalisation & schemes**: EPFO/ESIC coverage, Code on Wages & Labour Codes (4 codes, 2019-20), Skill India/NSDC, PMKVY, apprenticeship.
Disguised unemployment = hidden surplus labour in agriculture; PLFS is the data source.
Key rates: LFPR, WPR, UR; challenges = informality + low female LFPR.

prelimsPointers: **Disguised unemployment** — surplus workers whose marginal product is zero (common in agriculture).
**Types** — disguised, seasonal, structural, cyclical, frictional, educated/technological.
**Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** — official employment data (NSO, since 2017-18).
Indicators — **LFPR, Worker-Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR)**.
~**90% of the workforce is in the informal/unorganised sector**.
**Female Labour Force Participation** is low but improving.
'**Jobless growth**' — GDP rising without proportionate job creation — is a key concern.
Unemployment types: **disguised (agri), structural, cyclical, seasonal, frictional**.
Jobs data source = **PLFS (since 2017, NSO)**; gives **LFPR, WPR, unemployment rate**.
Concern: **low female LFPR**, informalisation; **e-Shram** for unorganised workers.
Four **Labour Codes (2019-20)**: Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, OSH.
mainsAngles: Analyse the nature of unemployment in India and its measurement.

glossary.definition: Situation where more workers are engaged than needed, with zero marginal productivity (esp. farming).
The Periodic Labour Force Survey, India's main source of employment-unemployment data.
Labour Force Participation Rate — the share of working-age population in the labour force.

blocks.text: India runs a large architecture of **employment-generation and poverty-eradication schemes** — the flagship **MGNREGA (rural wage-employment guarantee)** alongside skilling, self-employment, livelihood and social-security programmes — to secure inclusive growth.

rows: **100 days' guaranteed wage employment** to rural households; demand-driven; social audit.

blocks.text: Balanced **rural and urban development** is central to India's growth. Rural development tackles **agriculture, infrastructure, livelihoods and services**, while urban development addresses **housing, sanitation, mobility and smart infrastructure** amid rapid urbanisation.

rows: **PMGSY (roads), PMAY-Gramin (housing), Jal Jeevan Mission (tap water), Saubhagya (power)**.
**Smart Cities Mission, metro rail, urban transport**.
Rural — connectivity, credit, migration; Urban — slums, congestion, services, finance.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: rural & urban development

items: **Rural**: infrastructure (**PMGSY roads, PMAY-G, Jal Jeevan, SAUBHAGYA/DDUGJY power**), livelihoods (NRLM, MGNREGA), **Panchayati Raj** delivery, agri-marketing (e-NAM); challenges — migration, farm distress, connectivity.
**Urban**: **Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT (water/sewerage), PMAY-U, Swachh Bharat-Urban, HRIDAY, metros**; challenges — slums, solid waste, congestion, urban flooding, finance of ULBs.
**Balanced development**: rural-urban continuum, **RURBAN Mission (SPMRM)**, census towns, peri-urban growth.
**AP**: capital-region (Amaravati) urban plan; Vizag-Chennai corridor; rural welfare schemes; both agrarian and coastal-industrial development pushes.
Rural: PMGSY, PMAY-G, Jal Jeevan; Urban: PMAY-U, AMRUT, Smart Cities, Swachh Bharat.
Issues: rural connectivity/migration; urban slums/services/finance.
